title: Digital IDs can connect ASEAN
gist: The World Bank argues ASEAN should make national digital-identity wallets and verifiable credentials interoperable across borders under the DEFA framework, starting with mobile driving licenses, professional qualifications and business credentials, positioning Thailand as regional leader as it hosts the October IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings.

insights.claim: Verifiable credentials are digitally signed versions of trusted information such as driving licenses or company registrations, stored in a phone wallet and checkable instantly without consulting the source database.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Instant offline verification replaces slow paper and scan checks, cutting friction and fraud in cross-border transactions.
insights.quote: Verifiable credentials are secure, digitally signed versions of trusted information

insights.claim: A QR scan or NFC phone tap lets a credential holder share only what is needed, such as proof of being over a certain age instead of a full date of birth or identity.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Selective disclosure is a privacy-preserving design that could accelerate public adoption and regulatory acceptance.
insights.locator: A QR scan or phone tap

insights.claim: Almost every ASEAN country is developing a digital identity wallet, with Vietnam's VNeID exceeding 67 million accounts and Singapore's Singpass reaching 97% of eligible residents.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Digital-ID infrastructure is already at mass scale across ASEAN, so the marginal opportunity is interoperability, not new national systems.
insights.quote: Viet Nam’s VNeID has more than 67 million accounts, while Singapore’s Singpass reaches 97% of eligible residents.

insights.claim: Indonesia's national digital identity app IKD, supported by the World Bank, is used by more than 21 million citizens with a target of 100 million by 2029.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A near-fivefold user-growth target by 2029 signals sustained public investment in Indonesian digital public infrastructure.
insights.quote: It is already used by more than 21 million citizens, with a target of reaching 100 million by 2029.

insights.claim: ASEAN does not need a single regional wallet; aligned rules on trusted issuers, wallet communication, privacy, security and testing can connect national systems, much as linked payment systems support cross-border payments.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A standards-alignment approach avoids sovereignty conflicts and is more politically feasible than a centralized regional ID.
insights.quote: ASEAN does not need a single regional system or wallet.

insights.claim: By the end of 2026 every EU Member State is expected to offer a digital wallet built to common specifications, a model the article holds up as proof of what cross-border interoperability can achieve.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The EU precedent gives ASEAN a concrete template and timeline benchmark for common-spec wallets.
insights.quote: by the end of 2026, every EU Member State is expected to offer a wallet built to common specifications.

insights.claim: India now lets residents save an Aadhaar verifiable credential in Google Wallet for visa applications and identity checks, showing governments can remain the authoritative issuer while credentials work in third-party wallets.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Interoperability with private wallets expands reach without governments ceding issuer authority, a model for public-private digital-ID rollout.
insights.quote: India now lets residents save an Aadhaar verifiable credential in Google Wallet for visa applications

insights.claim: The World Bank recommends ASEAN start with cross-border mobile driving licenses, professional qualifications and business credentials, building on the Unique Business Identification Number initiative, before extending to more sensitive national identity uses.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A low-sensitivity-first sequencing builds trust incrementally, de-risking the politically harder national-ID stage.
insights.locator: ASEAN should act now, but in phases

insights.claim: IFC is investing in companies such as Malaysia's Zetrix AI to support digital identity verification and digital trade, alongside the World Bank's government-facing regional roadmap.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Private-sector capital is flowing into ASEAN digital-ID verification, flagging an investable segment tied to regional integration.
insights.quote: IFC ... is investing in companies such as Malaysia’s Zetrix AI to support digital identity verification and digital trade.

insights.claim: Thailand is positioned to lead ASEAN digital ID with ThaID exceeding 33 million users, ubiquitous PromptPay, and ETDA being the first in the region to develop a national verifiable credentials framework.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Thailand's mature digital public infrastructure makes it the natural hub, relevant as it hosts the October IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings.
insights.quote: ThaID has more than 33 million users, while PromptPay is ubiquitous.
insights.locator: Thailand is well placed to lead

insights.claim: The World Bank Group and Thailand are developing a Digital Compact to scale investment in digital transformation and AI for jobs, productivity and growth.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A formal Digital Compact signals a funding and reform pipeline for Thai digital and AI infrastructure.
insights.locator: This is part of a broader partnership
